title: Optimized Scratch Assay for In Vitro Testing of Cell Migration with an Automated Optical Camera.
markdown:
## Protocol: Optimized Scratch Assay for In Vitro Testing of Cell Migration with an Automated Optical Camera

### Overview

This protocol outlines the optimized scratch assay for in vitro testing of cell migration using an automated optical camera. The procedure involves preparing HaCaT cells, generating a confluent monolayer, performing mitomycin C treatment to arrest proliferation, creating a scratch wound, applying peptide stimuli, and capturing time-lapse images via software-controlled microscopy.

### Materials/Reagents

- DMEM media with 10% FBS and 1x antibiotics (penicillin and streptomycin)
- Mitomycin C stock solution (1 mg/mL) stored at 4 °C
- Working Mitomycin C solution (5 µg/mL and 10 µg/mL as needed)
- Peptide stimuli: Human and bovine Lactoferrin and Lactoferricin (tested at 25 µg/mL in 250 µL volume)
- 1x sterile PBS (calcium- and magnesium-free)
- 1x Trypsin

### Equipment

- T75 flask
- Pasteur pipettes
- Sterile laminar flow bench
- Conventional incubator (37 °C, 5% CO2)
- Optical microscope
- Hemocytometer or Coulter-counter
- Round-bottomed 48-well tissue culture plate (also compatible with 6-, 12-, 24-, or 96-well plates)
- 200 µL pipette tips
- Automated optical camera system with software interface

### Safety & Sterility

- Perform all steps in a sterile laminar flow-bench.
- Clean the bench and all equipment with 70% ethanol prior to starting the experiment.
- Ensure PBS is free of calcium and magnesium.
- Mitomycin C in solution can be stored up to one week in the dark at 2-8 °C.

## Reagent Preparation

### Preparation

1. Grow HaCaT cells in DMEM media supplemented with 10% FBS and 1x antibiotics (penicillin and streptomycin) in a T75 flask. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S01 -->
2. Prepare a working solution of 10 µg/mL mitomycin C in an appropriate amount of medium. Note: In this study, Mitomycin C is kept at 4 °C in a stock solution at 1 mg/mL. Mitomycin C in solution can be stored up to one week in the dark at 2-8 °C. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S02 -->
3. Prepare peptide stimuli by diluting them in an appropriate amount of medium. Note: In this study, both human and bovine Lactoferrin and Lactoferricin were tested at 25 µg/mL in a volume of 250 µL. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S03 -->

## Cell Monolayer Generation

### Day 0: Workspace Setup

1. Perform all subsequent steps in a sterile laminar flow-bench by cleaning the bench and all equipment with 70% ethanol prior to the start of the experiment. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S01 -->
2. Place the optical camera in a conventional incubator at 37 °C with 5% CO2 to ensure optimal conditions for the cells. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S02 -->

### Cell Detachment

1. Remove the medium from the T75 flask using a Pasteur pipette. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T1-S01 -->
2. Wash the adherent cells in the flask by adding 5 mL of 1x sterile PBS to the T75 flask. Note: Ensure that the PBS is free of calcium and magnesium. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T1-S02 -->
3. Circulate the PBS within the flask and remove it using a Pasteur pipette. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T1-S03 -->
4. Repeat step 2.2-2.3. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T1-S04 -->
5. Add 1 mL of 1x trypsin to the flask and disperse it across the cell layer. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T1-S05 -->
6. Incubate the flask at 37 °C in a conventional incubator until the cells are detached; 5-8 minutes is sufficient for most cell lines. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T1-S06 -->
7. View under the microscope to confirm cell detachment. Once detached, add 9 mL of regular culture media containing 10% FBS to inactivate the 1x trypsin. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T1-S07 -->

### Cell Counting

1. Count the cells using either a hemocytometer, a Coulter-counter, or similar device. Note: Trypan blue can be used to view dead cells; however, in 1x trypsin, HaCaT cells appear perfectly round when alive. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T2-S01 -->

### Seeding and Adhesion

1. Transfer 7.5 x 10^4 cells per well in 250 µL of 10% FBS media to a round-bottomed 48-well tissue culture plate (standard plate). Note: The assay can also be set up in 6-, 12-, 24-, or 96-well plates, which all can be assayed under the optical microscope. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T3-S01 -->
2. Gently move the plate from side to side to ensure the cells are equally spread in the wells, preventing them from gathering in the center. Inspect under a light microscope to verify that the cells are evenly spread in the media. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T3-S02 -->
3. Place the plate in a conventional CO2 incubator at 37 °C overnight or until the cells have adhered to the bottom of the wells. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T3-S03 -->

## Migration Assay Execution

### Confluence Check

1. Check if the wells are 90-95% confluent under a light microscope. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S01 -->

### Mitomycin C Treatment

1. Remove the spent media with a Pasteur pipette from each well. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T1-S01 -->
2. Add 250 µL of 5 µg/mL mitomycin C to each well. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T1-S02 -->
3. Incubate the plate for 2 hours at 37 °C and 5% CO2. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T1-S03 -->

### Washing and Scratching

1. Remove the medium containing mitomycin C with a Pasteur pipette. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T2-S01 -->
2. Wash the wells once with 250 µL of 1x PBS (room temperature) and remove the wash with a Pasteur pipette. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T2-S02 -->
3. Add 250 µL of 1x PBS and manually scratch the wells vertically with a 200 µL pipette tip. Use a new pipette tip for each well. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T2-S03 -->
4. Remove the PBS and add 250 µL of peptide stimuli. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T2-S04 -->

### Imaging Setup

1. Mount the plate in the optical camera system by adjusting the screws on both sides of the plate. Leave the lid on the microtiter plate. Note: The camera can operate with the lid open if necessary. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T3-S01 -->

## Software Configuration

### Program Setup

1. Click 'Acquire' in the taskbar on the left. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S01 -->
2. Choose the function 'Wound healing' in the taskbar on the left. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S02 -->
3. Choose the plate type by clicking below the Plate illustration. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S03 -->
4. Unselect wells not in use by marking them and click 'Enable' at the upper left side on the screen. Note: All wells are selected by default. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S04 -->
5. Adjust the focus of the lens on the wells to fit the position of the cells by right-clicking on one of the wells. Note: Autofocus can also be adjusted manually by moving the bar to the right of the plate illustration. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S05 -->
6. Set the time period for images under Picture Interval (e.g., 00:30:00). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S06 -->
7. Set the number of repetitions to fit the desired period (e.g., 97 repetitions). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S07 -->
8. Start the run by clicking the Start button in the lower right corner. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S08 -->

## References
